h2: NDT certification records management: what the auditor asks to see
html:
Every client audit, registrar visit and Level III review of an NDT company ends at the same file: the personnel certification records. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ANSI/ASNT CP-189 the employer certifies its own technicians, so the employer must be able to prove, for each person, method and level, that the requirements of its written practice were met. That proof is what NDT certification records management software exists to keep.

What each record has to hold

The written practice sets the detail, but auditors look for the same evidence in every file:

  • the method and level, and the technique where the written practice certifies techniques separately, such as phased array within UT;
  • training and experience hours, with the source of each: courses attended, on-the-job hours and who verified them;
  • results of the general, specific and practical examinations, and who administered and graded them;
  • the visual acuity examination for near vision and the colour contrast examination, each with its date, so the annual near-vision check cannot lapse unnoticed;
  • the certification and expiry dates and the signature of the Level III or other certifying authority;
  • any interruption of service, and recertification by examination or by evidence of continuing satisfactory work.

Why a spreadsheet stops being enough

A spreadsheet can list expiry dates, but nobody is warned when a technician whose eye examination lapsed last week books time on today's job, and it cannot show an auditor what changed and when. In the Certificates app each certificate's status is worked out every day, warnings go out well before anything expires, vision tests are records of their own linked to the technician rather than notes in a wallet, and timesheets warn when a technician books time without a valid certificate.

SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and ISO 9712 side by side

The record looks much the same under all three, but the rules differ. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice that each employer adapts in its own written practice. CP-189 is a standard with fixed requirements, including that the Level III holds an ASNT Level III certificate. ISO 9712 and the ASNT 9712 programme are central certification schemes, where an independent body issues the certificate and the employer still authorises the person to work. Recording the scheme on each certificate lets a mixed workforce be managed in one register. Our consultants can review the written practice behind the records, and NDT auditing services check the files themselves before a client does.

Where the records feed

Certification status is read by timesheets, by NDT report sign-off and by the rest of the NDT management software; equipment certificates follow the same pattern in calibration tracking. To see your own register in the app, request a demonstration.
